steps: A body is more stable when its centre of gravity is lower.
A body is more stable when it has a wider base.
Balancing toys are designed with a low centre of gravity, while racing cars are made low and broad to increase their stability.
items.finalAnswer: Stability is increased by lowering the centre of gravity and widening the base.

steps: In circular motion, the velocity of a body at any instant is along the tangent to its circular path.
The centripetal force is directed towards the centre of the circle, along the radius.
A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
Therefore, the centripetal force is always perpendicular to the velocity.
items.finalAnswer: Centripetal force acts along the radius, while velocity acts along the tangent; hence they are perpendicular.

steps: The car experiences more centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius.
For a body moving in a circle, centripetal force is given by F = mv²/r.
For the same car and the same speed, m and v are constant, so F is inversely proportional to r.
Thus, decreasing the radius increases the centripetal force. Therefore, the car experiences more force on the curve with the smaller radius.
items.finalAnswer: The car experiences more centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius.

steps: A ripe mango tends to remain at rest because of inertia of rest.
When the branch is shaken, the branch moves suddenly but the mango tends to remain in its original position.
The stalk is unable to hold the mango, so it breaks and the mango falls down.
items.finalAnswer: Due to inertia of rest, the mango tends to remain in place when the branch is shaken, causing its stalk to break.

steps: The stability of an object depends on the position of its centre of gravity and the size of its base of support.
An object topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base of support.
A lower centre of gravity makes an object more stable. For example, a low, broad racing car is less likely to topple than a tall, narrow one.
Widening the base of support makes an object more stable because the vertical line through its centre of gravity is more likely to remain within the base.
items.finalAnswer: An object is more stable with a lower centre of gravity and a wider base; it topples when the vertical through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

steps: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.
According to Newton’s second law, a non-zero resultant force produces acceleration.
Therefore, an accelerated body has a non-zero resultant force and cannot be in equilibrium.
items.finalAnswer: An accelerated body is not in equilibrium because the resultant force acting on it is not zero.

steps: The taller box is more likely to tumble over.
When the truck stops suddenly, each box tends to continue moving due to inertia of motion.
The retarding force of the floor acts near the base and produces a turning effect on the box.
The taller box has a higher centre of gravity, so this turning effect is more likely to make the vertical line through its centre of gravity fall outside its base.
items.finalAnswer: The taller box is more likely to tumble because its higher centre of gravity makes it less stable.

steps: The turning effect of a force about a point or pivot is called its moment.
Moment of a force = force × perpendicular distance of the line of action of the force from the pivot.
The principle of moments states that, for a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.
For example, a balanced see-saw is in equilibrium when the clockwise moment of one person equals the anticlockwise moment of the other person.
items.finalAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a pivot equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.
